column2: §YGlacial§!\nThe Glacial terrain represents areas with very harsh and cold conditions, often with permanent snow coverage and glaciers. Areas with Glacial terrain are almost completely inhospitable for settlement or military manoeuvres.
§YImpassable Mountains§!\nImpassable Mountains terrain represents areas of mountains too inhospitable or too difficult for an army to manoeuvre in.
§YMountain§!\nMountain terrain represents areas mainly occupied by rugged mountain ranges and narrow passes, often on high altitude and in a cold climate.
§YFarmlands§!\nFarmlands terrain represents highly cultivated areas where the landscape is dominated by agriculture and towns or villages.
§YGrasslands§!\nGrasslands terrain represents areas of farmland where the vegetation is dominated by grass.
§YCoastline§!\nCoastline terrain represents the narrow areas where land and sea meet, comprised of cliffs or sand dunes.
§YSteppes§!\nSteppes terrain represents large and continuous open areas covered in grass that are suitable for grazing yet unsuitable for agriculture.
§YDrylands§!\nDrylands, also known as badlands, represents large areas of barren, rocky and treeless flatland, often found at the edge of deserts or in particularly dry mountain valleys.

§YCraglands§!\nCraglands represent areas, often coastal, of extremely rocky and uneven earth. They often have little to no-vegetation and can prove hazardous not unlike reefs. They are particularly common along Morrowinds inner sea and along the Sheogorad region of Vvardenfell.
§YSavanna§!\nSavanna terrain represents large grass-covered areas with a high degree of trees mixed in.

§YHot Springs§!\nThere are many hot springs wherever volcanic activity is found. It is not uncommon to see Nords or Ashlanders soaking in these mineral-rich waters for their healing properties and comfort amidst the cold.

§YSalt Plains§!\nA salt plain occurs after the evaporation of a vast body of saltwater. Most salt plains in Tamriel are found along coastal lowlands. These lands are mostly vacant and harsh, but they do harbour rare minerals and make for great Saltrice plantations.
§YForest§!\nForest terrain represents areas of densely packed trees, lots of leaves and thick underbrush. The terrain can be difficult to see through and even harder to navigate.

§YFungal Forest§!\nNowhere is more famous for its Fungal Forests than Morrowind. Their presence is largely attributed to the humidity of the region and the warmth of Red Mountain. Fungal forests can grow as far north as Dagon Fel and as far south as Black Marsh. They are full of flora and fauna, and some of the region's rarest alchemical ingredients are found amongst these mushroom trees. Telvanni Towers and their surrounding plant cities are typically grown from a variant of these Fungi, whose growth is stimulated by soul gem magick and various other enchantments.

§YWoods§!\nWoods terrain represents a loose density of trees scattered around and light underbrush, with only pockets of density. They are easier to navigate than forests, and visibility is decent at a distance.

§YTaiga§!\nTaiga is a type of swampy coniferous forest only found in the far north. Their wood is durable and is used often in Nordic boat-making. Skyrim, Atmora, and Raven Rock are where most Taiga in Tamriel is found.

§YHills§!\nHills terrain represents areas dominated by a rolling landscape of shifting elevation that is lower and less steep than mountains. Unlike the highland terrain, hills represent areas with a higher density of trees and underbrush.

§YHighlands§!\nHighlands terrain represents areas dominated by a rolling landscape of shifting elevation that is lower and less steep than mountains. Unlike the hills, terrain highlands represent areas with a low density of trees and underbrush.
§YJungle§!\nJungle terrain represents areas overgrown with dense tropical vegetation, difficult for an army to manoeuvre in.
§YMarsh§!\nMarsh terrain represents tracts of wetland dominated by grasses or low-growing shrubs.

§YMudflats§!\nMudflats are coastal wetlands that form in inter-tidal areas where sediments have been deposited by tides or rivers. These regions are often found near lakes, rivers, bays and estuaries.

§YBayou§!\nThe Bayou is a swampy region with lots of trees and small patches of land. They are usually connected to a river or freshwater source flowing into them. In Tamriel, most Bayou can be found in Morrowind and Black Marsh. They are difficult to navigate and uncomfortable to live in, making them great spots for smuggling operations.
§YDesert§!\nDesert terrain represents desolate and arid areas with little or no vegetation, often in a very warm climate.
§YCoastal Desert§!\nCoastal Desert terrain represents areas where the desert meets the ocean, resulting in a milder and less inhospitable climate.

§YAshlands§!\nThe Ashlands are continuously created from the regular fall of ash from active volcanos, and the intermittent lava flows that rush down the ravines. Although they seem desolate, the Ashlands are teeming with various types of wildlife and tough plants, and they can fully support the Nomadic lifestyles of many people, including Velothi. Many Daedric temples are found in the Ashlands, and lesser Daedra often wander the region freely.

§YLava Flow§!\nAlthough for the most of the time, volcanos are dormant, they still have active lava flows in the immediate area. These regions are nearly impossible to traverse or settle but are full of rich metals fresh from Nirn's crust that make them appealing. Only the Dwemer knew how to permanently build in these regions safely, while the Ashlanders just nomadically roamed around them.

§YBarrow§!\nAtmorans and Nords bury their important dead according to tradition - A burial cavern is dug out, walls and doors built-in, then an important figure and his bodyguard are laid to rest alongside each other for their journey to Sovngarde. Often, Barrows are full of rare treasures, as well as Draugr - unliving ancestors come back to defend their Barrow.

§YDwemer Stronghold§!\nThe Dwemer, or People of the Deep, were a race of mer that preferred to live underground. The dwemer were adept at smithing and enchanting, enabling them to build large underground holds in some of the harshest terrain of all Tamriel, including Red Mountain. Some of the dwemer strongholds in Skyrim are known to connect to each other through the large underground networks that the Blackreach exposed.

§YRed Mountain§!\nRed Mountain is a massive volcano at the heart of the Vvardenfell isle. Although mostly dormant, the volcano still has active lava flows and foyadas that the lava rushes down from. This is the harshest environment to survive in all of Tamriel. Red Mountain is also known as The Red Tower, as it hosts the Heart of Lorkhan in its depths and is one of the Sixteen Towers upon which the reality of Nirn is built. The Dwemer named this region Vvardenfell, which means the City of the Strong Shield in the Dwemeris language.

§YMournhold§!\nMournhold - City of Light, City of Magic! Also known as the City of Gems and the City of Love and Charity. During the Merethic Era, Mournhold competed with Old Ebonheart to be the economic and political capital of Morrowind. After a single family, Clan Ra'Aathim gained control of both cities, Mournhold became the formal capital of the Chimer. Mournhold was also the capital city of the Tribunal God Almalexia and her Daedric anticipation, Boethiah.

§YKogoruhn§!\nKogoruhn means 'Unbreakable Home' in Aldmeris and was the fortress-city capital of House Dagoth. Originally, the region was a safe nomadic spot for the Dagoth Velothi tribe. However, with the invasion of the Nords and their Old Kingdom, a series of fortresses were commissioned around Vvardenfell to protect from the Nords, including Kogoruhn.

§YAld'Ruhn§!\nAld-Ruhn means Old Home in Aldmeris and was originally a neutral meeting ground for the Ashlander tribes. The settlement grew in and around the shell of a giant Emperor Crab, Skar, who was killed by Dranoth of House Hleran with the help of the four Ashkhans of the major tribes. The noble district of the city is located inside this enormous shell, referred to as 'Under-Skar'. Control of the city was contested between the Great Houses and Ashlanders, but in the 2nd Era, House Redoran took final control and began to formally expand upon the existing sprawl around Skar.

§YNecrom§!\nNecrom, or the City of the Dead, is where the most famous or influential Velothi is buried. According to Velothi tradition (and later Temple tradition), the remains of the deceased are typically cremated and placed in open burial pits for shrine worship or inside burial urns for preservation. Necrom has long been affiliated with the Indoril, the most devout worshippers of the Velothi.

§YNarsis§!\nNarsis-Where-All-Fervently-Praise-the-Prophet-Veloth, most commonly referred to as Narsis, is one of the original settlements of the Velothi. The building of Narsis marked the end of their long lifestyle of nomadic exile and slowly began the process of civilising the Velothi into the Chimer. This city was largely affiliated with the Hlaalu, who used its position near Argonia and Cyrodiil to become a trade centre.

§YTear§!\nTear has always been the home of the Dres, who gained significance from their very successful slave raids into nearby Black Marsh. Tear has long been known as the centre of the slave trade in Morrowind and, due to its proximity to Black Marsh, has never lacked slaves. The Dres established a fearsome legacy of trained Argonians whom they used as slave-hunters.

§YPort Telvannis§!\nPort Telvannis is the isolated island capital of the magical Telvanni. Partially grown and partially built by hand, the city is a shining example of Old Velothi architecture mixed with the uncontrolled fungal growth the Telvanni so love to build with. There are few laws here, as magical supremacy is the only true basis for determining who has authority. Port Telvannis has a hearty slave trade mixed with a vibrant economy of illegal and smuggled goods, all of which the Telvanni tolerate in the name of their independence and pursuit of power.

§YEbonheart§!\nEbonheart, also known as the Black City, has been described as the eldest city-state of Morrowind. It is the ancestral holding of Clan Ra'athim, a mixed-heritage Chimer-Nordic family whose wealth came from mining ebony in the region. Ebonheart was the first informal 'capital' of Morrowind and was where the first High Kingship was declared by Moraelyn Ra'athim shortly after pushing the Nords out of Morrowind in 1E416. Ebonheart was a rival of Mournhold during the First Era, competing to be the centre of Morrowind's politics and trade as well as the seat of the High King - when situations allowed for one. Although Mournhold 'won' the rival competition and became the capital, Ebonheart remained an economically powerful city well into the end of the 3rd Era. During these later eras, Ebonheart had an entire Argonian Quarter of the city where the House slaves lived. Permission was given for a Hist to be planted here as well.

§YNchardak§!\nNchardak was known as the 'City of a Hundred Towers'. It is recorded to be one of the largest and possibly most advanced of the Dwemer Archives, holding vast amounts of dwemer secrets within. Like most dwemer cities, Nchardak itself was a feat of engineering. Using a complex system of pipes and pumps, the hold was able to submerge and emerge its entrances to avoid invasion. Nchardak was also known as a major centre of military production - it was said to be capable of producing a single automaton every day, an achievement no other dwemer hold accomplished.

§YGalom Daeus§!\nGalom Daeus was most notably known for its observatory - the only of its kind to be built on Vvardenfell and one of but a few that the Dwemer were confirmed to have built across all Tamriel. As such, the hold itself would have been a major centre of astrological studies and was likely very closely connected to Kagrenac's broader study of metaphysical law. Dwemer's understanding of the cosmos was not just comprehensive but astounding in most circumstances - It is likely throughout history that only a handful of men and mer have understood as much as Dwemer did about Nirn's complicated universe.

§YKemel-Ze§!\nKemel-Ze, sometimes called the 'Cliff City', was one of the largest Dwemer holds ever constructed. The number of connected chambers suggests it was simultaneously a major centre of population, trade, production, and scientific studies alike. It's possible this city began as much smaller Dwemer holds that ended up merging into one conglomerate over time. The hold itself had a fabled Dwemer-built Observatory in its upper towers, of which only a few in Tamriel existed. Some signs indicate that the hold maintained a regular royal presence or dignitary of a distinguished Dwemer family - perhaps even some sort of 'reserved' quarters for when any ruling authority was visiting, whether they be Mage-Crafter, Dwarf-King or Ashlander Hortator. The most famous expedition into Kemel-Ze revealed a wealth-filled hidden chamber with a frieze on the wall which 'seemed to depict an ancient ritual of some kind, with a long line of classically-bearded Dwarven elders processing down the sidewalls, all seemingly bowing to the giant form of a god carved into the front wall of the chamber, which was caught in the act of stepping forth from the crater of a mountain in a cloud of smoke or steam.' - from 'The Ruins of Kemel-Ze'. This is an indication that some Dwemer here, likely powerful mage-crafters in positions of rank in society, were both aware of and a part of Kagrenac's plan surrounding the Anumidium and its construction.

§YBamz-Amschend§!\nBamz-Amschend was unique in its location, sitting right next to and eventually underneath the city of Mournhold. It is likely Mournhold started as a major trading centre near the entrance of Bamz-Amschend itself and then built over it after the Dwemer disappearance. Within Bamz-Amschend was a phenomenon of Dwemer engineering - the Karstangz-Bcharn, or 'Weather Witch' as some called it. This device was built during a time of drought and need, bringing rain to the region. It was a versatile device, able to manifest any type of desired weather in the region, including ash storms. This city was also responsible for the construction of Dwemer colossi Automatons, though may have only built them during the War of the First Council as a last-minute defensive measure.

§YForelhost§!\nForelhost served as a great monastery-fortress for the theocratic Dragon Cult based in Skyrim. Two Dragon Priests and their Masks were stationed here permanently - Rahgot and Vosis. At the end of the Dragon, War Forelhost served as the last holdout of those still loyal to the Cult. It fell to High King Harald, founder of the Kingdom of Skyrim, in 1E139. Before the besiegers could take the monastery, the remaining Cult members all committed suicide, leaving none alive for capture when the Nords finally came through the gates. A grisly scene awaited the attackers, signifying the end of the Dragon Cult's brutal reign in Skyrim.

§YFrulthuul§!\nFrulthuul was built by the Dragon Cult during their golden age of expansion. Its construction and architecture are similar to the Cult's other holdings found throughout Skyrim. In the 4th Era, it was occupied by Roscrea's Bear Cult.

§YTundra§!\nTundra is a type of flatland found in the far north. The growth of trees is hindered by low temperatures and short growing seasons. The soil is mostly frozen and rocky, sustaining only durable grasses and cold-weather crops. Without trees, there is no natural protection from the cold wind.

§YMountain Meadows§!\nThe valleys between high mountaintops experience a drier climate, which allows farming even at higher elevations. The Mountain Meadows offer both grassland and a defensive surrounding.

§YCaves§!\nCaves like all natural tunnels throughout Nirn are believed to be the capillaries of the world, pulsing with the divine essence of the Aedric earthbones. Practically they are narrow spaces which restrict visibility and movement. While often bountiful in ores and fungi, they are often dangerous locals.

§YSolitude§!\nSolitude is situated on the highland bluffs of Haafingar. The city is a major trading capital in the Sea of Ghosts, with an expansive and illustrious history that gives it its prominent political power. Solitude is the home of the Bards College, an institute that preserves the ancient Nordic traditions of music and story-telling, as well as Coterie of Organized Scholars, which was one of the oldest scholarly institutions in the region.

§YMarkarth§!\nKnown colloquially as the "City of Stone", Markarth is a former Dwemer city of Nchuand-Zel built through a large stone crag, intricately designed around the cliffs and waterfalls from the environment. Since the region is poor farmland, Markarth is mainly a mining town that has a vast influx of silver veins in the mountain. Since the city is the focal point of power throughout the region, it is often disputed over between the Reachmen and the Nords.

§YWhiterun§!\nWhiterun was founded in the late Merethic Era by Nords, who discovered the Skyforge. The city earned its name because it circles the running of the White River. Once a small community, now Whiterun is a thriving city, protected both by descendants of the ancient Nordic families and Kynareth pilgrims, who look after the Gildergreen tree, planted in the centre of the Wind District.

§YWindhelm§!\nWindhelm is one of the oldest cities in Skyrim, situated in the estuary of the White River. Windhelm was once the capital of the First Empire of the Nords, and the old Palace of the Ysgramor dynasty, the Palace of the Kings, still stands in the centre of the city. Despite being sacked multiple times, Windhelm always managed to rise and thrive again, becoming home not only for Nords but for many other races of Tamriel.

§YRiften§!\nRiften was built on the shores of Lake Honrich, nestled within the Fall Forest. Proximity to Cyrodiil and Morrowind made the city an important trade hub, which constantly generates high income for its owners. However, this also encouraged the growth of the criminal underworld, including the Thieves Guild, who nowadays controls Riften from the shadow.

§YDaggerfall§!\nDaggerfall is the largest city in Glenumbra, located at the southwestern end of the peninsula. It was found by Nords, who brought a rough sort of civilisation with them during the Skyrim Conquests. Nowadays, the city is the preeminent economic, cultural, and military force in southern High Rock, and some people think that this stance will not change for the next millennia.

§YCamlorn§!\nCamlorn is situated on the coastal highlands of Glenumbra. The city and the surrounding region are a melting pot of several different Breton cultures, and its people fancy themselves as more refined and metropolitan compared to their neighbours in Daggerfall. The Camlorn nobility considers themselves an aristocracy of poets and artisans, who greatly benefit from trade coming from either the Eltheric Ocean or the Iliac Bay.

§YWayrest§!\nWayrest is a major city in the centre of the Stormhaven region of High Rock, at the mouth of the Bjoulsae River. The city is split into seven districts: Residential, Merchant, Market, Temple, Palace, Banking and Docking. Today, Wayrest can boast the largest and richest population in High Rock.

§YShornhelm§!\nShornhelm is located in the centre of Rivenspire, acting as the seat of power for the Riven-King. The city is split between two districts: the lower city, where the common folk dwell and trade with one another, as well as the upper city, where the nobility live. Each of the noble houses has a manor in the district, as well as the local barracks and even the local wayshrine.

§YEvermore§!\nEvermore is a city on the banks of the Bjoulsae River in eastern High Rock, located near the border with Hammerfell. Its impressive Palace was assembled from slabs of granite quarried from nearby places. Local traditions include the worship of Saint Pelin, a hero of the First Era who once served as a clergyman at Bangkorai Garrison.

§YOrc Stronghold§!\nThe Orcish people are fond of an independent lifestyle of living. Instead of claiming one area, they would settle in multiple provinces depending on the preferences of each individual tribe. These orcs then build, tightly-knit strongholds and villages, some of which later turn into great and mighty citadels.

§YNorthpoint§!\nNorthpoint is located on the northeast point of Rivenspire. It is an important trading centre along the northwest trading route on the Eltheric Ocean, as well as the seat of power for House Dorell, one of the three major houses of Rivenspire. Their power extends across northern Rivenspire, including farmland around the city and beyond the sea.

§YFarrun§!\nFarrun is a city known for its icy winters. Situated in the Northern Wrothgar, it is a melting pot for various cultures, including orcs, bretons and reachmen. The mighty stronghold overlooking the city, as well as its remote location, has kept Farrun safe from many devastating wars, and although the city's power has changed many times, it is still one of the gems of High Rock.

§YJehanna§!\nJehanna is situated in the northernmost icy mountains of Wrothgar. Nestled in the snow-covered forests of the Western Reach, it is described as being as beautiful as its name. Nowadays, Jehanna is still an active settlement, providing a land bridge between Skyrim and High Rock for merchants and other travellers, who can arrive in the city both via land and sea.

§YDawnstar§!\nDawnstar is a settlement on the northern coast of Skyrim. It was once a small garrison town, which served as an exile post due to the cold, harsh climate and notorious gales, but now Dawnstar is the capital of Pale, famous for its mines and architecture. The city is also home to many fishermen and has an important port, providing a safe harbour for merchants travelling from Haafingar to Blacklight and vice versa.

§YWinterhold§!\nWinterhold is built on Hsaarik Head, the very tip of the Broken Cape and where Ysgramor first landed in Skyrim. It is surrounded by glaciers of the Ice Fields on virtually all sides, except the one facing the mountains. Winterhold is famous for its wealth, power, rich history and a school of the arcane arts.

§YMorthal§!\nMorthal is a fairly small, humble town of little economic or strategic importance besides its small lumber mill and a plethora of rare and useful ingredients available for sale. Sitting on the southern edge of the Drajkmyr marsh, dry ground can be hard to come by in Morthal and the city is often shrouded in a thick fog. Morthal's small population and relatively remote location have kept it distant from most major conflicts in its history.

§YFalkreath§!\nFalkreath is situated among boreal forest on a strategic crossroad. Because of this, many great battles took place there for centuries, and countless warriors were buried around the town, leaving behind graves and monuments to them. Nowadays, Falkreath is an important town for merchants and artisans, who, due to the nature of the city, are known to reflect the melancholic themes of death in their business.

§YBlacklight§!\nBlacklight sits in an advantageous trade position, being the most northerly port in Morrowind that all western sea trade passes through on its way east. It is also the most commonly used departure point for sailors and merchants making the rough journey north to Solstheim. At some point after the Great Houses emerged, Blacklight became the capital of House Redoran. During the 4th Era after the Argonian Accession War, Blacklight replaced Mournhold as the economic, political and administrative capital for the entirety of Morrowind.

§YBalmora§!\nBalmora translates as 'Stonewood' or 'Stoneforest' in Ald Chimeris, the language of the Chimer. The city was built in a rocky valley along both sides of the Odai River, positioned directly on a major north-south trade route. The joint river and road connections offered convenient access to the city and many beneficial trade opportunities. Over time, Balmora grew to become the second-largest city on the island of Vvardenfell, second only to Vivec. During the 2nd Era, House Redoran owned and developed the city, but through savvy political manoeuvring, House Hlaalu permanently came into possession of this profitable trade centre. Balmora was mostly destroyed in the 4th Era with the crashing of Baar Dau into Vivec, although rebuilding efforts took place after the devastation.

§YSadrith Mora§!\nSadrith Mora translates as 'Forest of the Mushrooms' in Ald Chimeris, the language of the Chimer. Located on the largest island of Zafirbel Bay, this Telvanni city was likely 'built', or rather 'grown', in typical Telvanni fashion, with stimulated magical growth being used on the local mushroom forest. The central Tower and epicentre of activity were Tel Naga, which housed the Archmagister of House Telvanni in the 3rd Era. Although not the capital of House Telvanni, it did serve as the seat of the Telvanni Council, given its convenient location to Vvardenfell and mainland politics. During the 3rd Era, the Empire built a large fort, Wolverine Hall, near Sadrith Mora in an effort to plug themselves into local activities as well as establish a north-eastern Tamrielic outpost for the Septims.

§YFirewatch§!\nFirewatch is said to be the closest 'major' mainland Velothi city to the peaks of Red Mountain. This trading port earned its name from the unobstructed and impeccable view of the volcano one has from the city. Firewatch's position on the northern tip of the Llothanis peninsula affords it convenient access to trade going through both the Inner Sea and the Sea of Ghosts.

§YAshen Wastes§!\nThe Ashen Wastes are a choking desert covered in ash that is constantly pushed forth from the surrounding volcanic peaks of the Deadlands. Visibility here is low due to the unsettled ash in the air. There are husks of many dead trees here, though it is unknown if any ever grew under Dagon or simply appeared this way. Compared to the rest of the Deadlands, the Ashen Wastes are some of the more stable areas to build in, lacking the constant volcanic activity of the other terrain.

§YSmouldering Badlands§!\nThe Smouldering Badlands are the flatter areas of the Deadlands full of decaying structures, withering plants, scattered fires and the occasional volcanic vent. Many things have been built here over time, only to be destroyed during the Dremoran wars or eventual volcanic destruction. It is easier to develop than most areas in the Deadlands due to the somewhat reliable stability of the terrain and distance from volcanic peaks.

§YBoiling Coast§!\nThe Deadlands is surrounded by an 'ocean' of lava that is constantly being filled by the unending rivers flowing from the volcanic peaks. The levels or 'tides' of the lava can rise and fall along the Boiling Coast, often accompanied by unpredictable lava waves. As a result, development of this terrain is difficult and costly.

§YBurning Hills§!\nThe Burning Hills are a collection of irregular lava rivers flowing through scattered foyadas. They flow downhill from the larger volcanic peaks of the Deadlands. Smaller vents emerging from the volcanic slope often push through in this difficult terrain, making development and travel through these provinces challenging and unappealing.

§YDaedric Keep§!\nDaedric Keeps are centres of authoritarian power throughout the Deadlands. Reflections of their Lord Mehrunes Dagon, these sharp and intimidating structures dominate the desolation of the Deadlands. They are operated by the strongest Valkynaz, who seizes control of the Keep, often being centres of militant slaving and planning the war with neighbours. During the Oblivion Crisis, the Daedric Keeps hosted the powerful Sigil Stones in the fortified upper room called the 'Sigillum Sanguis'. These Stones maintained the Oblivion Gates into Tamriel until closed by mortals able to enter into the Deadlands and manually destroy them.

§YVolcanic Peak§!\nThe Volcanic Peaks of the Deadlands are symbols of Lord Dagon Himself, violently and constantly changing the land with their enormous and infinitely destructive force. It is likely all mountain peaks in the Deadlands are volcanic, though not all are active. However, a formerly active peak can 'reignite' at any given time and reshape the land around it.

§YLava Cave§!\nVolcanic activity often creates underground caves in the surrounding region. These tubes are formed when flowing lava from a volcanic vent moves beneath the surface of a hardened lava flow. They are common in the volcanic areas, and some can be used to traverse from one area to another.

§YSulfuric Desolation§!\nThis caustic terrain is extremely rocky and full of stagnant sulfur pools. It makes navigation very difficult, and only the toughest Daedric weeds are capable of surviving here.

§YArdent Hope§!\nArdent Hope was a vast Daedric citadel in the Deadlands. It dominated control of the region and protected the Path of Cinders, which was the only ascent to Xarxes Crucible - a massive volcano in the region closely affiliated with Mehrunes Dagon and His favour.

§YMehrunes Dagon's Citadel§!\nMehrunes Dagon Himself often resides in His Citadel in the Great Lava Lake of the Deadlands. This fortress is nigh impregnable and is incredibly dangerous to any who dare assault it. When not found in His Citadel, Dagon is usually out personally inspecting his Xivilai and Dremoran slave-servants at their respective Keeps.

§YJynd's Foundry§!\nFounded by Dremoran Kynmarcher Jynd, here the Daedra supervise the study, design and construction of various relics, artefacts, magical devices and enchanted machines. The knowledge here is reserved for those who can seize and control the Foundry.

§YZynoahz's Gaol§!\nEstablished by the Xivilai Zynoahz, this jail primarily serves as a centre for the buying, selling and storing of slaves. Mortal souls who served Dagon in life are trapped in the Deadlands forever - enslaving these souls and forcing them to fight or work is common practise amongst the more powerful Daedra here.

§YWretched Spire§!\nOnce a part of Mournhold, the Wretched Spire was ripped from Nirn by Mehrunes Dagon in the first Era. The town is somewhat hidden in the sulfuric desolation of the Deadlands and is occupied by both Daedra and Dunmer alike working together to evade Dagon's malicious Will.

§YWorld Breaker§!\nThis massive fortress complex was one of Mehrunes' biggest in the Deadlands. One of its purposes was for the construction and storage of the 'Siege Crawler' - this enormous walking siege engine was imbued with immense fire magics and was used in Mehrunes' assault against Bruma during the 3rd Era Oblivion Crisis.

§YThe Razorworks§!\nThe Razorworks is a protected region used for a variety of smithing and crafting efforts by lesser Daedra, man and mer alike. Daring armourers, weaponsmiths and jewel crafters who desired to create the enchanted Deadlands Demolisher items would travel to this site to learn their protected smithing secrets.

§YVivec§!\nLikely populated as a trading port near the shrine of Ald Sotha, Vivec City truly started to appear after the rise of the Tribunal in the year 700. Once Vivec was declared Head of the Tribunal, He had a large semi-floating Palace 'canton' constructed in Norvayn Bay to create a new capital city from where He could live, rule and dream. As pilgrims frequented the location and the need for various services grew, additional cantons were constructed. By the 3rd Era, there were nine cantons connected by bridges and walkways, with a series of waterways between them all that allowed for further transport and mobility amidst the urban islands. Vivec City served as an economic and religious centre for the island of Vvardenfell during its long existence. The city guard was constituted almost exclusively of Temple Ordinators - Morrowind's most elite and feared warriors. Early on in its emergence, Sheogorath hurled a large meteor at the city in mockery of the Tribunal's so-called claim to 'Divinity'. Vivec stopped this rock, Baar Dau, where it remained frozen in momentum for thousands of years until it came crashing down thousands of years later after Vivec's disappearance, destroying the city in its entirety.

§YAlinor§!\nAlinor is the ancient capital of the Summerset Isles and the seat of High Elven civilisation. It is located on the temperate southwest coast of Summerset Isle, between the southern mountains and the idyllic beaches. Alinor is widely recognised by its sky-piercing towers and intricately woven ramparts that are designed to catch the light of the sun to break it into a variety of colours.

§YAnvil§!\nAnvil is a prosperous harbour city on the Gold Coast by the Abecean Sea at the very southwest end of Cyrodiil. Once, the city was just a small collection of ramshackle huts infamous for being a violent haven for pirates, refugees and thieves, but now Anvil attracts merchants and artisans from all across Tamriel and as far south as Pyandonea. Even though throughout its history, the city was besieged and almost ruined multiple times, Anvil always managed to restore its past glory, which in many respects was only possible thanks to the heroism and diligence of its inhabitants, who left behind not only high fortress walls but also magnificent temples and beautiful statues.

§YArchon§!\nArchon is situated on the eastern coast of the Black Marsh, surrounded by dense marshland. It is located near the coast, which makes it a perfect place to stop for merchants, following their path north to Morrowind or South to Lilmoth. Archon is also famous for its farmers, who manage not only to cultivate the land but also breed rare species of animals, such as the Glowgill Guar.

§YArenthia§!\nArenthia is situated in the borderlands of the northern Valenwood in the fork of both the Crescent and the Strid Rivers. The imprints of multiple cultures are evident in the history of the city, as well as in its architecture and the habits of the locals. Nowadays, Arenthia is an important trade city, famous for the production of vintage wines and musical instruments.

§YBlackrose§!\nBlackrose is located in south-central Black Marsh, among the pure waters of rivers and dense jungles. The history of this place is shrouded in darkness and keeps many secrets carefully guarded behind the high city walls. Blackrose is home to many peoples, from the Lilmothiit, who founded the settlement, to the Argonians and the Imperials, who claim authority over the city, which may have formed the basis of the mystique of the place, for each culture has tried to give the city something different, without being able to comprehend what others have already created.

§YBravil§!\nBravil is a merchant town located on the banks of the Niben Bay, in the estuary of the Larsius River. Originally founded by Ayleids, the city has seen many battles between Elven, Human and Daedric Armies, the result of which caused great destruction to the city and its residents, who have lost their lives either due to the hands of foreign invaders or fellow citizens, divided by barricades during another uprising. However, despite numerous attempts to destroy the city, Bravil has been rebuilt time after time, returning to its former glory and becoming a bridge between Cyrodiil and Elsweyr.

§YBruma§!\nBruma is located among the snow-covered peaks of the Jerall Mountains of Cyrodiil. A cold climate and proximity to Skyrim make the city a perfect place for Nordic merchants and settlers who want to make a fortune or start a new life. This is reflected in the city's architecture, which combines the traditions of the Nords, Nedes, and Elves to create a unique urban landscape.

§YCheydinhal§!\nCheydinhal is an idyllic and prosperous city situated in the boreal highlands. The town is known for its broad, green parkland and neatly trimmed cityscape, all of which surround the graceful willows of the Corbolo River. Cheydinhal's history recalls many conflicts with its neighbours and tragedies caused by the desire of its nobility to obtain power, but the passion of its residents to live in harmony with each other and other cultures lay a solid foundation for the further development of the city.

§YChorrol§!\nChorrol is a town in northwestern Cyrodiil, between the Great Forest of west Cyrodiil and the Colovian Highlands of the Hammerfell border. It is an important place both for merchants, who regularly organise fairies under the shade of oak trees and for scholars, who study various arts in the Academy of Chorrol. Nowadays, the city is protected by thick walls and guard towers, and even though there is a constant threat of earthquakes in the area, more and more people decide to settle in the suburbs of Chorrol.

§YCloudrest§!\nCloudrest is situated on the highest slopes of Eton Nir, the tallest mountain of the Summerset Islands. It is said that the ancient Altmer encountered creatures and prehistoric civilisations back when they first colonised Summerset and that the city of Cloudrest is a testament to these times, built in an odd mixture of different architectural styles with buildings like strangler vines, all of which built atop of older structures. Nowadays, Cloudrest is an important centre of power of Altmer civilisation, as it serves as headquarters for various prominent organisations and orders, including the Welkynar Gryphon Knights.

§YCorinthe§!\nCorinthe is located in the very heart of the Elsweyr on the edge of woodlands and savannah. The city has been known since ancient times for the art of its carpenters and builders. Despite various hardships that history prepared for Corinthe, its citizens managed to withstand the toughest of them and preserve their own culture through the millennia.

§YDragonstar§!\nDragonstar is situated on the foothills of the Dragontail Mountains just south of the border with High Rock and Skyrim. It is an important town for merchants who travel through the Reach Pass, miners who extract the Nirncrux from rich deposits, and mercenaries who offer their assistance to anyone who has a coin to spare. Being a very cosmopolitan city, Dragonstar opens its gates to everyone willing to start a new life and contribute to the prosperity of local communes.

§YDune§!\nDune is a prominent merchant town located among the savannahs of Anequina, which are generally known for their arid and dry climate. The city is built on a very large hill, which houses temples, markets, living quarters and various merchant camps. Being the capital of one of sixteen kingdoms, Dune is known for its priest, scholars and architects, who erected magnificent buildings to venerate the Two-Moons, Jode and Jone, which still please the eyes of citizens as well as foreigners, many of which visit the city nowadays.

§YDusk§!\nDusk is situated on the southeastern point of the Summerset Isle, at the place where the sun sets behind the mountain, leaving the town in a shroud of shadows. Buried deep in the mountains, west of Dusk, lies the Colossal Aldmeri Grotto, a vast cavern with ancient ruins that once served as the High Elven navy's watering spot. For a long time, the Dusk Keep was the only building in the area, overlooking the surrounding beaches and valleys, but nowadays, more and more people tend to settle around the fortress, being lured either by the desire to make a fortune or by pure curiosity, as Dusk is famous for a variety of Pale-Plume Gryphons, uncommon in the other regions of the Summerset Islands.

§YElden Root§!\nElden Root is the centre of the Wood Elven nation, situated in the southern heart of the Bosmer's great forests near a large lake. Most of the city itself is set throughout the branches and canopies of the Elden Tree, a legendary graht-oak, but there is also an outer district that runs along the eastern base of the tree, through the hills and the lake. Nowadays, Elden Root is not only a spiritual point of interest for many Bosmers, but the city also serves as a vast hub of trade and commerce, where many wealthy merchants and officials retain large-scale operations.

§YElinhir§!\nElinhir is one of the ancient cities of Craglorn, situated among the mountains near the border of Skyrim and Cyrodiil. It was originally founded by the Nedes, as evidenced by the city's tall Apex Towers. The towers rise above the impact site that was left by a great skystone that fell from the sky. Thanks to the powerful mages the city became a center of civilization in Craglorn, represented by it's architecture, markets and various academic buildings. Despite the constant threat of invasion coming from the Iron Orcs the city still prospers and acts as a bridge between Nordic and Nedic countries and people of all kinds.

§YFalinesti§!\nFalinesti, Colloquially known as the 'Walking City', is historically the capital of Valenwood, built from the Elden Tree. Narrow but solid streets of the city are always crowded by artisans, merchants and residents of Falinesti, whose homes are covered with curled webs of moss, which also form a roof. Nowadays, the city of Falinesti still plays an important role in the life of Bosmers, acting as a political, cultural and religious centre for the wood elves.

§YFirsthold§!\nFirsthold is built on the highest point of Auridon, among the vernal groves and craggy cliffs. The city is surrounded by high walls, behind which gleaming spires and royal parks are built around the Diceto River, calm waters which flow through the centre of Firsthold. This city is the centre of magic and science on Summerset Islands as it houses the headquarters of the Mages Guild and the Great Orrey of Firsthold.

§YGideon§!\nGideon is one of the prominent cities in Black Marsh, surrounded by steep hills and humid marshlands. Its cobbled streets are lined with grand, ornate buildings that have seen the civilisations of mer, men and beastfolk rise and decline. Visitors to the city of Gideon will find themselves captivated by its beauty and charm, as in this place, time seems to stand still.

§YGilane§!\nGilane, situated on the northern edge of the isthmus in Khefrem, is a bustling trade city which attracts merchants from various parts of Tamriel. It is also home to a large library, where scholars come to study the history and culture of Hammerfell. Gilane is a vibrant city full of life and is a melting pot of different races, which offers a unique experience for anyone who decides to visit it.

§YGreenheart§!\nGreenheart is situated near the southern coast of Greenshade. It is a walled settlement built upon magic-made cliffs and giant trees, which support Altmer-style buildings. Crowning Greenheart sits the Tower where the Throne of the Wilderking is, made from both marble and living magic-shaped trees.

§YHaven§!\nHaven is situated in the dense marshes of southeast Grahtwood in a strategic location on the coast of the Southern Sea. Despite frequent storms, the city is a major trading post, connecting the sea routes between Auridon and Elsweyr. In addition to merchants, Haven also entices artisans of all sorts with its numerous and easily accessible mineral deposits, including various rare shells highly prized among jewellers, alchemists, and sagas.

§YHegathe§!\nHegathe is found on the west coast of the province, on the southernmost point of the area considered part of the Alik'r. Like other traditional cities in Hammerfell, it is built atop old ruins of past civilisations, replaced with high domes and flying dew sails that are well-suited for the harsh environment. Hegathe is known for its bustling trade, its beautiful architecture, and its vibrant nightlife.

§YHelstrom§!\nThe city of Helstrom is located in the impenetrable central swamps of Black Marsh, among dense jungles and dark-water rivers. However, a number of unique shops and markets, tucked away in a bizarre maze of streets, entice traders and adventurers from Cyrodiil to Morrowind to set out despite the dangers and difficulties. The fortunate few who make it to the city walls in one piece may get the chance to take part in one of the many local festivals, the roots of which can be traced back to a time when the Hist trees were only just settling their seeds.

§YImperial City§!\nThe Imperial City is situated in the centre of Lake Rumare, surrounded by lush forests and beautiful hills. The city is known for its majestic architecture, grand palaces, and bustling markets and is home to a variety of cultural and historical sites, including the Imperial Palace, the White-Gold Tower, and the Arena. Visitors to Imperial City can spare their own time in a wide range of gardens, shops and taverns, eagerly awaiting to be explored.

§YKvatch§!\nKvatch is built atop a large bluff, raising the city above the surrounding forests, inhabited by a variety of wildlife, including bears, wolves, and foxes. The city itself is known for its architecture: the magnificent temples and monuments, among which the Kvatch Arena holds the first place. However, what makes Kvatch truly unforgettable for every visitor is its inhabitants - skilled craftsmen who produce some of the finest weapons and armour in all of Cyrodiil, wise wizards who are always happy to offer magical services and training to those who seek them, and hospitable traders who welcome every stranger from whatever part of Tamriel they may come.

§YLeyawiin§!\nLeyawiin is situated in the mouth of the Niben River, where it opens into Topal Bay. The city is one of the largest cities in the region and serves as a major trading hub between Elsweyr, Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. Nowadays, Leyawiin is a prosperous metropolis filled with merchants, artisans, adventurers of all kinds, powerful mages, mighty warriors and just for travellers seeking fortune or a safe haven to finally get away from danger and hardship, so common in every part of Tamriel.

§YLillandril§!\nLillandril is situated on the western hills of the Summerset Isle, where the land gives way to the ocean to form the lowland and sunken basin. The city is known for scholarly pursuits - various institutes such as the College of Sapiarchs and the Illumination Academy were both found in the vicinity of high Lillandril's walls. Nowadays, the city is a major trading port and is a popular destination for adventurers and merchants of many different races and cultures, making it a truly diverse and welcoming place for everyone who is tall and has golden skin.

§YLilmoth§!\nLilmoth, known as the 'Festering Jewel of Black Marsh, is a prosperous trading city governed by a council of powerful merchants. Lilmoth is famous for its exotic architecture, as it is built upon a network of canals, bridges, and platforms. Docks and wharves play a special role in the life of the city, as citizens and visitors gather there to buy and sell their wares, celebrate the foundation of a new ship or just discuss the most recent rumours meanwhile eating or drinking food sold there as well by local traders.

§YOrcrest§!\nOrcrest is built atop a plateau that overlooks the harsh desert of the Scar, providing a stunning view of the surrounding landscape with ancient walls and great bridges across the canyon. The city is known for its expansive bazaar, where merchants from all parts of Anequina can sell their goods, and a massive town hall, the owner of which to this day is considered the legitimate ruler of Orcrest. Various temples, houses and small shops that form a labyrinth of streets in the shadow of this hall attract numerous visitors every day, who have come to the city of Orcrest in search of an unforgettable experience.

§YPort Hunding§!\nPort Hunding is a prosperous port city located on the island of Stros M'Kai, a strategical location off the southern coast of Hammerfell near the Cape of the Blue Divide. The city is known for its architectural monuments, among which the most prominent is a large metal statue of Frandar Hunding, with his sword extending out to sea, and Three Princes Statues, standing over the Regent's Pool. Port Hunding is home to numerous merchants, sailors, and adventurers, who trade, explore, or just wander winding streets, visit the ancient ruins, or take in the breathtaking views from the harbour.

§YRihad§!\nRihad is a sprawling port city, built on the top of ancient ruins in the mouth of the Brena river. The city is known for its busy markets, active even during sunless nights, and its vibrant culture, formed by numerous merchants, artisans and adventurers, who consider this place their home even if they were born in distant lands. Rihad attracts visitors from all over High Rock and Cyrodiil, as it offers a unique opportunity to experience the local lifestyle without the need to embark on long and hazardous journeys inland towards the high mountains or the vast deserts.

§YRimmen§!\nRimmen is an oasis in the harsh lands of Elsweyr, as tropical plants and trees grow on artificial canals that flow from the great Anequine aqueducts. This made the city one of the most attractive spots for visitors, which has greatly contributed to the development of a major trade and commerce centre that can compete with the influence of Bravil, Leyawiin and Mistral. Rimmen is also a major cultural centre, with many festivals, events, and performances taking place throughout the year, during some of which everyone is welcomed to the royal castle, overlooking the city, where the King and Queen of Anequina originally lived.

§YRiverhold§!\nRiverhold is the gateway into Elsweyr, found along the streams and waterfalls of the Larsius River in the region of Anequina. The city is famous for its impressive architecture, swarming, and overcrowded marketplaces, specifically the Market of Fresh Delights, which encompasses the centre of the town and various workshops, where everything from weapons and armour to furniture and jewellery can be created. Citizens of Riverhold are also known for their strong sense of community, which is reflected in the many festivals and celebrations organised every year.

§YSenchal§!\nSenchal is found in the southern rainforests and river basins of Elsweyr, on strategic grounds in the coastal highlands of the Quin'rawl Peninsula. The city is famous for its crowded bazaars, open-aired markets and one of the largest ports on the whole Tamriel, in the harbour area of which thousands of merchants, artisans, smugglers and pirates live. The jewel in Senchal's crown is the Palace, built on a hill overlooking the harbour and the city itself, with its houses, towers and gardens lining the central square.

§YSentinel§!\nSentinel is located in the northwestern hills of Hammerfell between the warn waters Iliac Bay on one side and vast Alik'r Desert on the other. The main street of the city houses the great market, which stretches from the crowded docks, where hundreds of merchant ships from High Rock are awaiting their turn to be unloaded, and the front gates protecting the city at troubled nights. Many great and famous people throughout history have called Sentinel their home, and every visitor to this city can understand them after sampling the exotic cuisine, buying local handicrafts or enjoying a theatre performance in one of Sentinel's many amphitheatres.

§YShimmerene§!\nShimmerene is a dense, seaside city built on a hill that overlooks the Auridon Strait, the large body of water that separates the main island from Auridon. The city has only one entrance in its western wall, a long stairway from the main road, from where a breathtaking view opens at narrow streets, confined together by high walls and arches. Shimmerene is famous for many architectural masterpieces, among which the most notable is the Monastery of Serene Harmony, a large temple and centre of divine worship in the city.

§YSilvenar§!\nSilvenar is situated in the primordial jungles of Valenwood, on the banks of the Xylo River. It is a city of unrivalled beauty, known for its magnificent shades of coloured trees, combined with an intricate web of translucent amber that coats streets and bridges, above which tall minarets and spires built from marble rise up to the sky. A special part in the layout of Silvenar is devoted to the Audience Hall, described as an enormous dome that meets at the top and thin rays of light come down, where various ceremonies featuring the Silvenar and the Green Lady take place.

§YSkaven§!\nSkaven is a large and sprawling metropolis, many parts of which are located underground to be protected from scorching rays of sunshine that pour from the sky day after day. The city is known for its tunnels, catacombs and chambers, where citizens are able to hide from the unpleasant weather or the enemy forces, which have always desired to take the 'Jewel of Sunforge'. Skaven stands apart from other Hammerfell cities due to its unique culture and atmosphere that was raised since the end of the Merethic Era, but those who are brave enough to embrace the differences are going to discover the unique history of this place is reflected in the walls of ancient temples, on the shelves of local libraries, among the many scrolls and in the arenas where the best warriors of the city demonstrate their martial skills.

§YSkingrad§!\nSkingrad is the largest city in the West Weald, situated among rolling hills and lush forests. The city is famous for its wines, tomatoes, and cheeses, which contribute to its overall prosperity, but the citizens are particularly proud of the various architectural monuments that form the aesthetics of Skingrad and include the Great Chapel, the Guild Hall and the Castle. Skingrad's strategic location on the border of Elsweyr and close to the source of the Strid River has made it an important trading centre, where merchants from across Tamriel, from Hammerfell in the west to Morrowind in the east, can meet to exchange their goods, drink aged wine in local taverns and hire a few mercenary companies for protection on the return journey.

§YSkywatch§!\nSkywatch is an ancient port city built upon cliffs bordered by sparkling sea and surrounded by old Aldmeri fortresses, the most famous of which is Hightide Keep. The city is known for its beautiful architecture, especially its grandiose Palace, located atop the western cliffs, and various spires that form the skyline and are built in orthodox Altmeri style among elegant fountains and manicured gardens. Moreover, Skywatch is home to a large number of merchants, traders, and craftsmen, who day after day work hard to maintain the prosperity of their city.

§YSoulrest§!\nSoulrest is a quiet port town that leaves the crashing sound of the sea behind its gates. The city is known for its many gardens and parks, which are popular places for locals and visitors alike to relax and enjoy the natural beauty of the city, and its coastal access brings it a vast influx of foreign goods and aesthetics that merchants from distant lands bring to the market, situated right near the docks. Soulrest is a perfect place for anyone who is tired of the rhythm of big city life and wants to spend as much time in nature as possible without leaving the safety of the high walls.

§YSouthpoint§!\nSouthpoint is a major trade port of southern Valenwood, known for its markets, where wine from Cyrodiil neighbours moon sugar from Elsweyr, and fishing industry, capable of feeding every citizen and visitor. The city is surrounded by lush vegetation and low hills, which over time begin to be replaced by less and less passable forests. Southpoint is the home for thousands of merchants, who are ready to travel to distant lands for exotic goods, fishermen, who spare more time at sea than on land, and farmers, who day after day work on small chunks of fertile soil that surrounds the city.

§YStormhold§!\nStormhold is situated near the banks of a mighty river that forms the provincial border between the primordial morass of Black Marsh and the scenic grazelands of Morrowind. It is one of the biggest settlements in Black Marsh, surrounded by sunken marshes and crocodile-infested ravines with shallow waters, atop which Stormhold buildings reside, protected by high walls. Stormhold is known as a city with a dark history that features horrors of wars, hunger and slavery, but despite that, it still lures merchants, warriors and simple adventurers by opportunities that a lucky soul can take advantage of this centre for commerce, military craftsmanship and archaeology.

§YSunhold§!\nSunhold is a major city found behind the natural barrier of the southern mountains of Summerset Isle, buried deep in the forests on the coast. The city is known for its narrow winding alleyways, labyrinthine streets, tall, impenetrable sea walls that have dealt with centuries of constant assault by various enemy forces, and one of the largest harbours, which is considered the heart of shipping in the Tamriel. Every visitor of Sunhold can't resist the beauty of this place, highlighted by impressive architecture, with towering spires, grand palaces, and ancient monuments.

§YTaneth§!\nTaneth is situated among rocky perilous highlands and barren canyons, with ancient tombs hidden from the open. This city is known for its strong military tradition, maintained by a number of influential warrior clans that have always played a crucial role in the life of Taneth during war times. However, in less challenging situations, the life of the city centred around a harbour and port where ships came from every corner of Tamriel, laden with goods to be carried on camels' humps for further transport across the sun-scorched deserts and plains to the peaks of the Dragontail Mountains.

§YThorn§!\nThorn is located on the very edge of Black Marsh swamps, between the humid wetlands and salt plains. The city is known for its large system of canals that split Thorn into multiple districts, connected by wooden bridges, that time to time are which are occasionally washed out to sea during another storm. Much of the townsfolk are busy trading with neighbouring Morrowind, harvesting the seafood that comes ashore in rough seas or gets caught in fishing nets, or farming, trying to gather a few harvests a year to sell at the local fairs held several times a year.

§YTorval§!\nTorval is situated between jungles and rainforests of Elsweyr, under the protection of a large garrison of city guards, who are on duty day and night both in impregnable towers and in the surrounding villages, providing security and peace of mind to all the inhabitants of the neighbouring lands, who concentrate on trade, farming and livestock breeding. Thanks to this, while commerce is booming in the city, farming and livestock breeding are flourishing outside of it. Every visitor to Torval remains impressed by the beauty of its architecture, crowned by the Mane palaces and their surrounding gardens, where from time to time one can watch how both wise priests and eminent warriors meditate in the shade of thick leaves.

§YWoodhearth§!\nWoodhearth is a prominent coastal city, situated among lush forests of Valenwood in proximity to swamps of Shademist Moors and Rootwater Grove. The city is known for its skilful artisans, who craft everything from jewellery and pottery to weapons and furniture, and hard-working builders who do their best to erect new structures in maximum harmony with the natural surroundings. The citizens of Woodhearth are happy to welcome everyone who is just as passionate about nature as they are and have the will to contribute to the maintenance of the peaceful and measured life of the city.

§YAbbarbas§!\nAbbarbas stands on a white-sand beach at the mouth of a kelp-choked channel, overseen by a prince indebted to King Orgnum. As Pyandonea's busiest maritime entrepot, the markets of Abbarbas brim with gold-traded sea-serpent mounts, coral-carved trinkets, and the soft beat of membranous sails. Each dawn, a rolling veil of mist storms sweeps across the coral breakwaters, muffling the clamour of sailors who return back to ships after a night spent at taverns until the first light reveals serpent scales of sea snakes rushing into the depths of Pyrrahn Bay.

§YSecula§!\nSecula perches atop a green plateau, towering over the vast desert around it. Despite the surrounding barrenness, hidden springs feed lush gardens that thrive within the city's walls, offering refuge to craftspeople and hunters alike. Interlaced walkways link timbered halls where artisans tempt the traders with the most exquisite crafts beneath veils of fog while hunting parties of fishermen prepare to set out at dawn to capture a couple more of the mighty sea serpents, yet to be tamed.

§YEtho Sul§!\nEtho Sul clings to a coastal mangrove fen on the island to the north of Pyandonea's mainland. A lattice of elevated causeways and tide gates weaves through the mangroves, channelling the brackish tides into the city's reservoirs and permitting the clergy to perform their daily offerings to hungry serpents venerated as sacred animals. Etho Sul itself could be separated into two parts: the port, populated by numerous fishermen boats and merchant ships, and the city, where residences of high-ranking clergy are dotted around parks and temples dedicated to the immortal Serpent King.

§YKituna Vos§!\nKituna Vos sprawls across the coral flats that form a fragile connection between the city and the island of Vos across the strait. During the day, the streets of Kituna Vos are crowded with craftsmen who sell magical talismans, delicate clothes and exquisite armour. However, at night, when the sun's blazing heat is replaced by a warm wind, lantern-lit boats leave the safe harbour of Kituna Vos to hunt fish, crabs and serpents lurking in the dark of the sea waters.

§YWega§!\nWega is situated on the doorway to deep jungles that stretch across Pyandonea, separating its northern desert from southern hills. Wega's sprawling markets brim with crates of plum wine, jars of jungle honey, and other commodities, ready to be transported between jungle settlements and coastal cities. However, the true heart of Wega is located in its bustling harbour, where merchant barges are moored next to dozens of warships that constantly patrol the waters of Pyrrahn Bay in search of pirates and potential prey.

§YArch§!\nArch is the principal port city on Yokuda's western coast, where towering breakwaters deflected the fierce storms coming from the open sea. Arch's shipyards know no rest, assembling both merchant and wartime vessels under the constant clamour of hammer on steel as master smiths forge reinforcing bands for ship hulls from orichalcum-alloyed iron. At the heart of the waterfront, a sprawling bazaar spills over the docks, its stalls heaped with salted fish from nearby coves, intricately carved coral jewellery, and exotic spices that attest to Arch's far-reaching maritime trade.

§YTotambu§!\nTotambu is the capital of Yokuda and the anchor of political life on Akos Kasaz. Its grand domed halls and soaring columns house steel-plated Cartularies that record the names of Ansei warriors, who proudly maintained the shifting balance between sword-singer orders and provincial warlords. Dominating Totambu's highest terrace stands the grand temple of Tu'whacca, where ceremonies venerating Caretaker of the Far Shores are conducted on a regular basis.

§YMakan§!\nMakan is a major port town, famous for architecture of its wooden docks and stone storehouses, that cling to wind-scoured cliffs of Yath, an island, known for its arid, rocky terrain and vast open vistas under an unrelenting sun. The settlement also serves as an important naval base for Yokuda's coastal patrols, and its fortified quays and signal towers ensure the security of shipping lanes against raiders and privateers. Beyond its military role, Makan's taverns and charter halls bustle with mercenaries and sellswords, drawn by promises of fortune and glory on offshore expeditions across the Sea of Pearls.

§YLumut§!\nLumut occupies a narrow strip of black-sand beach on the volcanic island of Kanesh. Its bustling markets trade in polished rubies, obsidian fragments, and the famed brittle glass forged from cooled lava flows. Lumut's natural lava-reef breakwaters form a sheltered bay that offers a safe harbour to ships seeking refuge from the devastating storms that sweep across the Sea of Pearls.

§YTagon§!\nTagon rose around a clear spring nestled at the western coast of Akos Kasaz. The city's whitewashed buildings and domed caravanserais fan out like a great sunburst among the wind-swept grasses. Each spring transforms Tagon into a riot of colour and motion, as horse-lords challenge one another in mounted archery, horn-blowing contests, and ritual prayers to the Herd-Mother beneath the azure sky.

§YYul§!\nYul is a modest caravan hub on the central plains of Akos Kasaz, where overland trade routes converged on a network of fortified waystations. Ancient texts record Yul simply by name, with few details surviving about its original architecture or inhabitants. Nevertheless, despite its scant mention in the annals of Yokuda, Yul's dusty crossroads to this day are teemed with laden camels, wandering bards, and traders haggling over silks, spices, and steppes' furs beneath the weathered arches of city's ancient gatehouses.

§YGreymoor Keep§!\nGreymoor Keep is one of Blackreach’s largest constructions, that since the late Merethic Era has been serving as a vampyric stronghold. Its massive walls and buttressed ramparts climb the cavern’s rock face until they touch the vaulted ceiling above, forging an imposing silhouette beneath the ancient city. Inside, endless corridors and spiral staircases wind through blood-stained courtyards and vaulted halls, lit by flickering brazier flames that cast dancing shadows across the keep’s iron-forged gates and ominous battlements.

§YSilent City§!\nThe Silent City is the crowning achievement of Dwemer engineering, constructed at the centre of the Blackreach cavern. The city's vaulted halls, spiralling towers, and aqueduct arches carved from basalt and reinforced with Dwemer metal rise above the surrounding caves, releasing a soft blue glow from the luminescent mushrooms. However, the true heart of the Silent City is located beneath its foundation, where a network of cisterns and conduits channels Blackreach's subterranean rivers to power numerous machines operating in the city.

§YDusktown§!\nDusktown is a mining town situated deep in the cavern of Blackreach. The town's narrow streets wind between sturdy lodgings hewn directly from stone walls, while a cluster of workshops ensures that the ores burrowed deep beneath the earth are constantly extracted, melted and refined. However, the main feature of the city is its atmosphere, created by a combination of the constant movement of local residents rushing to work or to the tavern and emphasized by the eternal twilight, formed by luminescent mushrooms and only occasionally illuminated by sparks from the impact of bricks on the particularly durable rock.

§YHollow City§!\nHollow City is a once-grand Ayleid metropolis located in the heart of Coldharbour. Its soaring spires, prism-tinted glass windows, and marble-clad plazas stand frozen in spectral light while the surrounding wastes writhe in eternal darkness. Beneath its luminous ramparts, broad, empty boulevards fan out from a central citadel, flanked by elegant colonnades and silent statues that whisper of past times and faded civilizations.

§YLightless Oubliette§!\nLightless Oubliette stands among Coldharbour's Shrouded Plain, erected under the order of the God of Schemes as a bleak counterpart to the White-Gold Tower. Oubliette's corridors and cells are intentionally suffused with absolute darkness, with wardens forbidding ordinary light and resorting only to cold-spectrum illumination to prevent prisoners from channelling their magical powers. Within the iron-barred depths of Lightless Oubliette, the stifling void swallows every tortured whisper and distant scream, serving as a perpetual reminder of Molag Bal's merciless dominion over suffering.

§YHaj Uxith§!\nHaj Uxith is an Argonian town stranded in the Shrouded Plain of Coldharbour, anchored around a colossal Hist tree. Brought to Molag Bal's realm during the events of Duskfall, the town still preserves the spirit and soul of an era when the cities of Black Marsh rose above pristine jungles, although much of its former charm has withered amid the endless swamps and wastes that surround it. Nevertheless, Haj Uxith's narrow streets still snake through vaulted reed chambers, hosting communal halls, artisan workshops, and hidden sanctuaries where scholars quietly safeguard ancient knowledge.

§YReaver Citadel§!\nThe Reaver Citadel stands astride the craggy heights of Coldharbour's Fist of Stone, a fortress forged from the bones of an Imperial city dragged through the Planemeld into Molag Bal's realm. Obsidian ramparts and monolithic walls, etched with Daedric sigils, encircle a shattered urban sprawl where Dremoras patrol streets and squares while the Reaver pyramid looms like a black star in the sunless sky. Beneath the Citadel's battlements lie the forsaken halls, now twisted into prisons, torture chambers, and testing grounds, where countless souls have disappeared to feed the insatiable hunger of their masters.

§YContempt Court§!\nThe Court of Contempt is a Daedric citadel, where towering obsidian pillars and shadow-slicked corridors converge on its infamous Hall of Judgment, where the mortals are observed by soulless magistrates, tested by restless Dremoras and judged by the Court to determine their worthiness in serving Molag Bal. Citadel's vast yards are hemmed in by monolithic walls, while ever-burning braziers cast dancing shadows across cracked marble floors scarred by the passage of countless captives. They sink into the earth through spiral staircases, sealing off hidden dungeons where the clanking of chains and the distant roar of tormented serve as constant reminders of the Citadel's unbreakable grip.

§YQuey§!\nQuey is an important trading hub and one of the few bigger urban centres of the Cathnoquey archipelago. Being located in a remote region of Nirn, the residents of Quey are self-reliant out of necessity. In the city's markets, one can find every tool, weapon, food and other supply needed, with the occasional gold jewellery and fine clothes all crafted in local workshops.

§YBlack Harbor§!\nThe most important trading hub in the northern parts of the Spice Islands, Black Harbor holds influence in Akavir far beyond its borders. The city holds a monopoly on trading a number of elusive and highly sought-after spices. Whether it's merchants from all corners of the continent who seek a chance for a single purchase, envoys who desire to curry favour with the city councillors, or mercenaries who strive to work for the city's famously rich ruling class, you will find all manner of races and cultures here dreaming about the wealth Black Harbor is synonymous with.

§YYneslea§!\nYneslea is the dominant trading hub of the southern Spice Islands and the most prominent rival of Black Harbor. Using its wealth to bribe, sway and threaten the smaller cities near it, the city managed to steer the all-important spice trade to itself, further cementing its position. Yneslea's markets are always full of merchants and customers, and they also have quite a few shady characters who will find no shortage of work here.

§YJylkurfyk§!\nAt the southern edge of Atmora lies the major trading and shipping hub of Jylkurfyk. Its location makes it an almost necessary stop for any trader heading towards the north-western part of the continent, filling its marketplaces with loud haggling as they eagerly buy all the necessary supplies needed to survive the journey. The city's shipping industry is further boosted by its relative proximity to Tamriel, making it the most important hub for any brave traveller seeking to undertake the perilous journey across the Sea of Ghosts.

§YForelgrim§!\nForelgrim is a bustling and notorious trading hub situated at the eastern entrance of a dangerous, narrow sea passage. This passage offers a shortcut to the north-western parts of the continent that bypasses all of Southern-Atmora. Frequently used by merchants who wish to avoid the myriad of tolls imposed by the local chiefs and shady characters who wish to conduct business with minimal attention, the markets of the city face no shortage when it comes to customers or goods of all nature.

§YDragon Sanctuary§!\nDeep within the hard-to-access centre of Atmora, surrounded by frozen wastelands and rugged highlands, lies Dragon Sanctuary. As the most sacred site and political centre for the Dragon Cult, its frigid districts house numerous temples, altars and all the necessary lodging for the dragon priests and their servants. In the city's outer rings, a vast number of workshops provide all the necessities its residents need.

§YTsaesci§!\nThe first city of the Tsaesci people, now the political centre of their race, Tsaesci is located on multiple islands at the entrance of the Bay of Serpents. The administrative, residential, temple and port districts are all located on separate islands, with ferries providing the only connection between them. As the main base of the Tsaesci's unrivalled fleet, the shipyards of the city work all day, every day, while the markets are filled with thousands of customers haggling for any ware the continent has to offer.

§YIonith§!\nThe political centre of the south-western edge of Akavir mainland, Ionith is located in a large patch of fertile mountain meadows. The surrounding mountains and hills provide the city with decent protection against both windstorms coming from the southern sea or invaders. Being a major supply hub for armies, the city's workshops make a decent living supplying weapons, armour, food and all manner of goods needed by the soldiers, who protect Ionith to ensure its continued prosperity.

§YUmsiuesci§!\nA harbour town located at the eastern edge of Marzonia, Umsiuesci is a major entrepot for all the exotic goods harvested from the surrounding jungles. The city's location makes it ideal for exporting these goods to the many Tsaesci holdings to the south and east. Umsiuesci's harbour is also a prime resupply hub for traders coming from the Spice Islands before they make their way to the inner regions of Akavir.

§YShaesci§!\nA spiritual centre at the coast of the Bay of Serpents, Shaesci is one of the most ancient cities of the Tsaesci people. It is here where the tenants of the Tsaesci Order were formulated, and the numerous monasteries, shrines and arenas dedicated to Ilni, Myn, Nyfa and Zisa can be found. Warriors, mages, monks and all manner of people visit the city to prove themselves against each other in often deadly duels in the various arenas or the streets, all dreaming about gaining fame and receiving an invitation to the annual Grand tournament held here.

§YTzuosci§!\nTzuosci was originally a mighty fort, established to maintain control over the nearby islands, and thus the only safe sea route of Southern-Akavir. Built in a generally inhospitable region, the garrison's family members, servants, and the craftsmen following the army settled what lands they could near the fort, setting the foundations of the city we see today. Nowadays, the mighty coastal fort is still the beating heart of Tzuosci, while the residents make a living supplying the soldiers, harvesting the resources of the nearby jungles and catching all kinds of fishes in the murky waters of the nearby bay.

§YEoryuesci§!\nLocated in proximity to the Po Tun lands, the city of Eoryuesci is the bastion that protects the Tsaesci heartlands. The city and its surroundings are filled to the brim with major and minor fortifications both on land and along the coast, prepared to face attackers from every direction. The districts of Eoryuesci are stripped of any luxuries that would waste space. If there was a place for a theatre, one would probably find barracks or regimental camps there instead.

§YTosh Raka§!\nTosh Raka is a proud and ancient city with a rich military history. Ancient rival with the Tsaesci city of Eoryuesci, it serves almost the same purpose. Being the primary staging ground for raids and the first line of defence against Tsaesci attacks, the two settlements almost grew together as the never-ending hatred of their respective races fueled more and more resources into building them up. Tosh Raka's beating heat is the massive fortress and all the forges, armouries, and barracks that supply the garrison.

§YJhaotun§!\nProtected by a great river from the south and east and massive mountains from the north and west, the city of Jhaotun prospers despite its many hostile neighbours. The settlement became the largest over time for the Po Tun people, having far-reaching influence due to its sheer economic might. Whether it's humble fishing, mercenary jobs or any form of craftsmanship, one will find no shortage of opportunities here to make a living.

§YDar'hax§!\nDar'hax is the largest urban settlement of the Canis-men. Its location as a natural harbour, the richness of the nearby mines, the relative fertility of the land surrounding it and the plenty of fish in its waters ensured that the city naturally became a metropolis. One can find workshops of all varieties, multiple marketplaces and all services the weary traveller can request. The large population and the close proximity of hostile neighbours make Dar'hax a formidable centre of military might as well.

§YJianhax§!\nJianhax is a major port and pirate heaven at the coast of the Kamali Gulf. Located in a prime position to intercept ships sailing the narrow pass that splits the continent of Akavir in half, lonely merchants have little choice but to pay the toll, providing a steady revenue for the settlement. The residents often supplement farming and fishing with piracy, so any buccaneer captain will find no crew shortage here should the need arise.

§YPo'hax§!\nContrary to her sister town, Jianhax, to the north, the port town of Po'hax is a peaceful trade hub. Its location and the relative fertility of the nearby lands make it a natural supply hub for any merchant sailing towards the Thousand Islands or Kamal, who eagerly buys all the food nearby farms provide. The residents are mainly animal breeders, who tend to their herds in the large savannas surrounding the settlement and sell their produce to the many merchants in town.

§YTang Mo§!\nThe city of Tang Mo is one of the largest urban centres in the Thousand Islands. The main landmark is a massive arena where hundreds of tribe leaders gather during emergencies to discuss the details of the defence. The settlement mostly consists of residential districts to help accommodate all the leaders and their followers, while the various workshops and service businesses stockpile in advance to manage the sky-high demand of the meetings and survive until the next one with the fortune they make during these events.

§YKoda§!\nKoda is the most prominent trade hub in the Tang Da region. The settlement's location is somewhat protected from southern windstorms and has easy access to all the other regions inhabited by the Tang Mo race. The city has one giant and very noisy marketplace with warehouses, the harbour and a great number of houses.

§YUmpa§!\nUmpa is a major military town, home to many warrior-monk orders. Since the resident's motto is: 'Walls don't stop the enemy, warriors do', the city boasts surprisingly weak fortifications.
